entryPoint: SLA::sendAlerts() — include/class.sla.php lines 99-101. Zero-argument instance method on the SLA ORM model (extends VerySimpleModel) that reports whether overdue-alert notifications are enabled for `$this` SLA plan. Current body: `return 0 === ($this->flags & self::FLAG_NOALERTS);` where FLAG_NOALERTS = 0x0004 (a class const shared with FLAG_ACTIVE=0x0001, FLAG_ESCALATE=0x0002, FLAG_TRANSIENT=0x0008).
coreLogic: The entire core logic is the single expression `0 === ($this->flags & self::FLAG_NOALERTS)` — a strict-identity comparison (===) against the bitwise AND of the instance's flags column and the FLAG_NOALERTS bit. Unlike its sibling SLA::priorityEscalation() (already extracted in MOD-26, which has a pre-existing `&&` vs `&` bug), this method uses the correct bitwise `&` operator and a strict `0 ===` check, so its semantics exactly match the intent: true means the bit is clear (alerts enabled), false means the bit is set (alerts disabled). There is no sub-delegation inside sendAlerts() itself — it is a pure inline-expression method, same shape/pattern as isActive() and isTransient() in the same class.
consumers: SLA::alertOnOverdue() (include/class.sla.php, lines 113-115): `function alertOnOverdue() { return $this->sendAlerts(); }` — a direct, unconditional delegation wrapper with no other logic. This is itself a facade-adjacent method, not the extraction target, and must keep calling sendAlerts() (or the patched facade) unchanged.

Ticket::onOverdue($whine=true, $comments="") (include/class.ticket.php, line ~2121): `if ($whine && ($sla = $this->getSLA()) && !$sla->alertOnOverdue()) $whine = false;` — the only real call site across the codebase (found via a full-repo grep for sendAlerts|alertOnOverdue; no other matches besides the method definitions themselves). If sendAlerts()/alertOnOverdue() returns false, $whine is forced false, which short-circuits the rest of onOverdue() and suppresses the overdue-alert emails that would otherwise be sent to department members/staff further down in that method. Ticket::onOverdue() and all of ticket.php are explicitly out of scope for this ticket — only the boolean contract consumed here must be preserved.

include/class.filter_action.php line 264 has a comment only (`# XXX: Does this imply turning it on as well? (via ->sendAlerts())`) — not an executable call site, just developer commentary; no action needed.

include/class.filter.php line 224 defines an unrelated `Filter::sendAlerts()` method on a completely different class (Filter, not SLA) — a naming collision only, not a caller of SLA::sendAlerts() and out of scope for this seam.
inputShape: None — sendAlerts() takes zero parameters. It reads only `$this->flags`, an int column on the SLA_TABLE row already hydrated into the SLA instance by VerySimpleModel (either via a DB lookup/fetch, or via `new SLA(array('flags'=>$n))`, which sets the property in memory with no DB query).
outputShape: Returns a plain PHP boolean (the result of the === operator, always type bool). Exact contract to preserve: true iff `$this->flags & self::FLAG_NOALERTS` is exactly 0 (FLAG_NOALERTS bit clear — overdue alerts enabled); false iff that bitwise AND is non-zero, i.e. FLAG_NOALERTS (0x0004) is set (overdue alerts disabled), regardless of which other bits are also set. No mutation of $this or any argument; pure read, new boolean value returned, nothing passed by reference.
sideEffects: None within sendAlerts() itself: it performs a pure read of the already in-memory `$this->flags` property. No DB query is triggered by this call — VerySimpleModel hydrates the full row (including flags) when the SLA object is constructed/looked up, before sendAlerts() is ever invoked.
No global state ($cfg, etc.) is read or written by sendAlerts().
No lazy-loading, caching, or file I/O occurs in sendAlerts().
alertOnOverdue() adds no additional side effects — it is a pure one-line delegation to sendAlerts().

Out-of-scope context only (facade-adjacent, NOT part of what gets extracted): the sole real consumer, Ticket::onOverdue(), performs significant side effects downstream of this boolean (querying dept/staff, sending alert emails via $email->sendAlert(), etc.) but those live entirely in include/class.ticket.php and are explicitly excluded from this extraction per the ticket's isolation rules.
constraints: Preserve the existing method signature exactly: `sendAlerts()` takes zero arguments and returns a plain bool, callable on an SLA instance exactly as `$sla->sendAlerts()` is today.

Preserve the exact boolean return semantics: strict `0 === ($flags & FLAG_NOALERTS)`. Lift this expression verbatim into the extracted service rather than rewriting it as an equivalent-looking form (e.g. `!($flags & FLAG_NOALERTS)`) — same discipline already applied for the sibling SLA::priorityEscalation() extraction (MOD-26), even though this method has no known bug to preserve.

Per the anti-recursion rule, the extracted service must never call back into SLA::sendAlerts() or SLA::alertOnOverdue() — it must take the already-hydrated flags int (and the FLAG_NOALERTS bit value) as parameters and return the lifted boolean expression directly (lifted-logic pattern, same as SlaPriorityEscalationChecker).
SLA::alertOnOverdue() must continue delegating through the patched sendAlerts() unchanged — do not inline or bypass that delegation as part of this ticket.
No new DB reads/writes may be introduced — the flags value must be passed in already-hydrated, exactly as `$this->flags` is read today, with no re-fetch.

The extracted service must reference SLA::FLAG_NOALERTS (or receive the flags int and the FLAG_NOALERTS constant value as inputs) rather than hardcoding the literal 0x0004, so it stays correct if flag bit values are ever renumbered.

Must not alter the behavior of Ticket::onOverdue() (out of scope) or any other ticket-overdue/assignment logic — only the sendAlerts() boolean contract it consumes may be touched, and only via the facade patch.
Do not touch the unrelated Filter::sendAlerts() method in include/class.filter.php — same method name, different class, not part of this seam.

Do not edit include/class.team.php, include/class.dept.php, include/class.topic.php, or include/class.ticket.php, and do not extract addGracePeriod, priorityEscalation, isTransient, or any ticket overdue/assignment behavior — all out of scope per the ticket's isolation rules.

flags=0 (no flags set) must return true; FLAG_NOALERTS alone (flags=4) must return false; FLAG_NOALERTS combined with other SLA flags (e.g. FLAG_ACTIVE|FLAG_NOALERTS=5, or FLAG_ACTIVE|FLAG_ESCALATE|FLAG_NOALERTS=7) must return false; the all-flags upper bound (FLAG_ACTIVE|FLAG_ESCALATE|FLAG_NOALERTS|FLAG_TRANSIENT=0x000F=15) must return false — these are the required fixture cases per the ticket's acceptance criteria.
harnessInputShape: JSON object with a single field: `flags` (int) — the raw SLA.flags bitmask value to test on an in-memory SLA instance (constructed via `new SLA(array('flags' => $input['flags']))`, which sets the property with no DB query). The harness calls `->sendAlerts()` on that instance and echoes {input, output} where output is the boolean result. Suggested cases per acceptance criteria: flags=0 (no flags — alerts enabled, expect true), flags=4 (FLAG_NOALERTS only — alerts disabled, expect false), flags=5 or flags=7 (FLAG_NOALERTS combined with other SLA flags, e.g. FLAG_ACTIVE|FLAG_NOALERTS=5 or FLAG_ACTIVE|FLAG_ESCALATE|FLAG_NOALERTS=7 — alerts disabled, expect false), and flags=15 (0x000F — all four flags set, the upper-bound all-flags case — alerts disabled, expect false).
